review_notes: Read the whole file and checked Mathlib's StronglyMeasurable/Lemmas.lean. It has only the fixed-vector `apply_continuousLinearMap` lemmas, and I found no existing two-argument `clm_apply` measurability lemma. I also grepped other EnergyForm files for reuse. The other lemmas are thin wrappers around `continuous_energyIntegrand.comp_*`, so I did not flag them. The repeated block is the 'evaluate a measurable field of bilinear forms on two measurable vectors' argument. It appears in three proofs, once more in the strong version. I have not compiled the proposed generic lemma, so the exact instance requirements are unchecked. It should need only normed-space structure, since `Continuous.clm_apply` is stated for general normed spaces.

findings.problem: The same argument is written three times, each with its own `have hcont`/`hc`. A measurable field of continuous bilinear forms `φ x : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ` is evaluated on measurable fields `u x, v x` by composing with the continuous map `(φ,u,v) ↦ φ u v`. The strong version (lines 36–46) and the a.e. version (lines 104–115) have identical continuity proofs. They differ only in the `comp_stronglyMeasurable` / `comp_aestronglyMeasurable` finish. `aestronglyMeasurable_matrixBilinearForm_apply` (lines 117–125) repeats the a.e. argument for another bilinear-form type, using `fun_prop` for the continuity. The file therefore has two proofs of the continuity of this evaluation map (one manual, one by `fun_prop`) and three copies of the compose-with-`prodMk` step. The local `let Jet := …` is also needed only to state `hcont`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two generic lemmas near the top of the file, for a normed space `E` over ℝ:

`lemma stronglyMeasurable_clm_apply₂ {φ : α → E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ} {u v : α → E} (hφ : StronglyMeasurable φ) (hu : StronglyMeasurable u) (hv : StronglyMeasurable v) : StronglyMeasurable fun x => φ x (u x) (v x)`

`lemma aestronglyMeasurable_clm_apply₂ {φ : α → E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ} {u v : α → E} (hφ : AEStronglyMeasurable φ μ) (hu : AEStronglyMeasurable u μ) (hv : AEStronglyMeasurable v μ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => φ x (u x) (v x)) μ`

Proof sketch for each lemma: have `hc : Continuous fun q : (E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) × E × E => q.1 q.2.1 q.2.2 := by fun_prop`, as already done in lines 120–121, with `Continuous.clm_apply` as the manual fallback. Then `exact hc.comp_stronglyMeasurable (hφ.prodMk (hu.prodMk hv))`, or the a.e. analogue.

Rewritten uses, under the same hypotheses:
- `stronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand_apply₂ … := stronglyMeasurable_clm_apply₂ (stronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand ha hb hc) hU hV`
- `aestronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand_apply₂ … := aestronglyMeasurable_clm_apply₂ (aestronglyMeasurable_energyIntegrand ha hb hc) hU hV`
- `aestronglyMeasurable_matrixBilinearForm_apply … := aestronglyMeasurable_clm_apply₂ ha hη hξ`

The fixed-jet `_apply` lemmas are unchanged, since they already go through `_apply₂` or `apply_continuousLinearMap`.
findings.benefit: The continuity of `(φ,u,v) ↦ φ u v` and the compose-with-`prodMk` step are proved once per measurability notion instead of three times. The three public lemmas become one-line applications. This removes the `let Jet` and `hcont` boilerplate and the inconsistency between manual and `fun_prop` proofs. A future strongly-measurable matrix-form lemma would also be a one-liner, and any change to the argument is made in one place.
